name: Fracture Drift
description: Fracture Drift is a genre built on the principle of stratified listening: a single piece contains between four and nine distinct compositional layers, each accessible only at a specific level of auditory augmentation. A baseline human hears a spare, melancholic acoustic piece — often featuring live instruments like prepared guqin, mbira, or nyckelharpa. A listener with standard consumer-grade chrome augments hears an additional layer of sub-bass frequencies and ultrasonic harmonics that transform the piece's emotional texture entirely. Military-grade or high-end Tier 4/5 augments unlock further layers: polyrhythmic structures composed in frequency ranges that unaugmented ears register only as pressure, neural-overlay melodic lines that interact directly with the BCI's auditory cortex mapping, and at the highest augmentation tier, a final layer that composers describe as 'the interior' — a deeply personal melodic statement designed to feel private, as if composed for the listener alone. The genre emerged around 2207 from collaborative workshops between acoustic instrument revivalists and augmentation modification artists in the upper Circuit.
creator: various
audience: Deliberately cross-tier by design philosophy. Shelf and low-Circuit listeners with no augmentation experience the acoustic layer genuinely and completely. Augmented listeners at every level hear a different piece. This makes Fracture Drift politically complicated and culturally beloved — the same recording means something different depending on your body.
cultural_impact: Fracture Drift became an accidental political flashpoint because it made augmentation inequality audible and literal. Activists on the Shelf use it as a demonstration tool: play a Drift piece, then explain that the chrome-wealthy are hearing something richer, more complex, more beautiful — and that this is true of their entire lives. The genre's founders have repeatedly insisted this was not their intent, but the metaphor proved too perfect to contain. Vantablack Media subsidiaries have released polished Fracture Drift albums for the Tier 4 and 5 market while the underground scene remains the genre's creative heart. There is ongoing tension between commercial co-optation and the scene's original cross-tier idealism.
known_fans: augmentation modification artists and chrome-body subculture
Shelf activists who use it as a political metaphor
Tier 4 audiophiles who collect high-augment-layer recordings
neural engineers who study the compositional technique
story_hooks: A Fracture Drift composer has hidden something in the ninth layer of their final album — not music, but a data packet. Only someone with illegal military-grade auditory augments can hear it, and word has gotten out that it exists. Multiple factions are now hunting both the album and anyone with the chrome to decode it.

A Shelf activist organizing around Fracture Drift's inequality metaphor is approached by a Vantablack Media talent scout who wants to sign them — not to suppress their message, but to monetize it, which might be worse.
A character with damaged augments can no longer hear the upper strata of Fracture Drift pieces they once loved. The loss is both personal and a constant reminder of what their injury cost them.
